The test image shows a corn leaf with elongated, narrow tan/cream-colored lesions running parallel to the leaf veins. The lesions are rectangular, vein-bounded, and pale tan to whitish. This pattern strongly suggests Gray Leaf Spot.

Let me check one reference image to confirm.

The reference shows advanced Gray Leaf Spot (coalesced lesions causing whole-plant blighting). The test image shows the earlier stage — narrow, rectangular, tan lesions bounded by leaf veins running parallel to the midrib. This is the classic presentation of Gray Leaf Spot before lesions coalesce. The morphology matches well.
